clue.text: It's not important, ballroom dance's repeats both being foxtrot

indicators.note: the repeats being something else means they are replaced by it

parts.note: the cha-cha-cha is a Latin ballroom dance
the two repeated syllables after the first one

indicators.note: both repeats become foxtrot, so the letter is doubled

parts.note: Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dance teacher dismisses a routine whose repeated steps have all been swapped for foxtrot moves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foxtrot' looks like another dance but is the radio code for F. In CHA-CHA-CHA the two repeated CHAs are each replaced by F.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is worthless husk, so figuratively anything trivial: something that is not important.

clue.text: Jokes, mostly personal, causing degradation

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: comedy is jokes collectively
own means personal, belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: Telling personal jokes leads to humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a fall in status or dignity, a humiliating loss of standing.

clue.text: Ecstasy within completely horrific symbolism

parts.note: all means completely, as in all wrong
gory means bloody and horrific
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled vision full of utterly horrific imagery.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events stand for deeper meanings, extended symbolism.

clue.text: I'm impatient and always drink to stay bluff

indicators.note: to stay is to prop up; in a down clue the drink sits below the bluff supporting it

parts.note: for good means forever, always
a ness is a headland, a bluff
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A bluff, gruff type who always drinks to keep up appearances, tired of waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' looks like an adjective, hearty, but is a cliff; 'stay' means support, not remain.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is uttered in exasperation, expressing the speaker's impatience or annoyance.

clue.text: Sontag maybe framing small criticism about once sacred mountain

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the whole string is read backwards
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: Susan Sontag was the American essayist, so Sontag stands for her first name
a rap is a rebuke or criticism

explanation.surface: The critic Susan Sontag writes a mild critique of a mountain once held holy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' sets the small letter after the first three of the essayist's first name, and 'about' turns the whole string round; 'Sontag maybe' signals a first name, not the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Parnassus in Greece was sacred to Apollo and the Muses in ancient times.

clue.text: Boxer receiving left punch

indicators.note: receiving means the boxer word takes the letter in

parts.note: pug is short for pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer takes a left hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' could be the dog breed, and a pug is another dog, but here it means a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug someone is slang for hitting them, delivering a punch.

clue.text: Fundraiser set up over there involving an O'Connor, say

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means written upwards, reversed
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: yonder means over there
taken as written
Des O'Connor was a British TV entertainer and singer

explanation.surface: Someone organises a charity event over there featuring a celebrity called O'Connor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' and 'set up' work on the whole phrase, so the comedian's name ends up backwards too. Red Nose Day is the UK Comic Relief charity telethon.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Nose Day is a biennial British charity event raising money through comedy and plastic noses.

clue.text: Air-traffic control is unsuccessful at keeping fourth in proximity

parts.note: ATC is the abbreviation for air-traffic control

indicators.note: keeping means the losing word holds the other inside it

parts.note: loses means is unsuccessful
a quarter is a fourth part

explanation.surface: Air-traffic controllers fail to keep the fourth plane at a safe distance.
explanation.definitionFit: At close quarters means very near, in close contact or proximity.

clue.text: Second subject to split in books

parts.note: under means subject to, as in under orders

explanation.surface: A second topic causes a rift in the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunder is a literary, archaic word for split apart, found mainly in written texts.

clue.text: Hound satirical writer penning piece central to column

indicators.note: penning means the writer's name encloses the other letters

parts.note: Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro, writer of satirical short stories

indicators.note: piece central to means the middle letters of the word column

explanation.surface: A satirist savages someone in a column he is writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a verb for harassing but is the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The saluki is a slender Middle Eastern sighthound breed.

clue.text: Route for deliveries of sort run in barrow?

indicators.note: in means the sort-and-run pair sits inside the barrow word

parts.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound
ilk means sort or kind
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what kind of route a wheelbarrow delivery takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrow' suggests a wheelbarrow but means a burial mound. A milk round is the British milkman's daily doorstep delivery route.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk round is the regular route a milkman follows delivering bottles to homes.

clue.text: Duct conveying liquid tin and other metal

parts.note: a tin is a can
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Describes a pipe carrying fluid made of tin and another metal.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a canal is a tubular passage, such as the ear canal, carrying fluid.

clue.text: Perhaps sly male's function: steer around girlfriend

indicators.note: the function and steer words sit around the girlfriend abbreviation

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

explanation.surface: A cunning man's role is to guide someone around his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steer' reads as a verb but is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Foxes are proverbially sly, and a dog fox is the male of the species, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Isolated inside pit with collar to wrap throat

indicators.note: inside means the isolated word goes within the pit word

parts.note: a pock is a pit or scar in the skin
lone means isolated or solitary

explanation.surface: Someone stuck alone in a pit clutches a collar around their neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo neck is a high, close-fitting turned-over collar on a sweater that covers the throat.

clue.text: French wine label to tear up, which was driven from interwar years

definitions.text: which was driven from interwar years

parts.note: vin is French for wine
a tag is a label

indicators.note: up in a down clue means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: to tear is to race or rush

explanation.surface: A French wine's label is ripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tear' reads as rip but means rush. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a vintage car is one built between 1919 and 1930, a motor from that era.

clue.text: Lord ruined in Great War, returning to get married, provides many pages with connections

indicators.note: in places the rearranged lord letters inside the war abbreviation

parts.note: WWI is World War One, the Great War

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the word lord are wrecked and rearranged
returning means the phrase for getting married is read backwards

parts.note: to be wed is to get married

explanation.surface: A lord ruined in the First World War comes home to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' scrambles the peer, 'in' sets him inside the war, and 'returning' turns the marriage phrase round. 'provides' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The World Wide Web is the vast system of hyperlinked pages on the internet.

clue.text: Jar containing letter that is covered in pencil

indicators.note: containing means the jar word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to grate is to jar or rasp
phi is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A jar holds a letter that has been scribbled over in pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' looks like IE, but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphite is the soft carbon forming the core of a pencil, encased in wood.

clue.text: Stuff that's fabricated and somewhat obscenely retold in turn

indicators.note: in turn means the selected letters are read backwards
somewhat means only part of the words obscenely retold is used

explanation.surface: A tale of fabrication retold in rather obscene fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ENELYRET lies within 'obscenely retold' and is read backwards. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Terylene is a synthetic polyester fibre, a man-made fabric material.

clue.text: Fighting words in Chirac's resignation statement?

definitions.text: Fighting words in Chirac's resignation statement?

parts.words: Fighting words in Chirac's resignation statement?
parts.note: a French phrase meaning that's war, used as a resigned shrug, which a French president such as Jacques Chirac might say

explanation.surface: Imagines a former French president announcing he is stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resignation' suggests leaving office but means accepting fate; 'Fighting words' are literally words about war.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression, literally 'that is war', is said with weary acceptance of misfortune.

clue.text: Soldier possibly supporting old court sector

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means placed beneath the other letters

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant, so an ant may be a soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier perhaps backs a former court division.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is one-eighth of a circle, a sector of 45 degrees.

clue.text: First-class society to delight in

parts.note: to lap up something is to enjoy it eagerly

explanation.surface: High society relishing the best things.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-up is a British informal term for a lavish, excellent meal: top-notch.

clue.text: Clubs justify storing case of labels for identification of station

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: storing means the align word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: to justify text is to align it

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: Instructions for laying out playing cards and labels at a station.
explanation.definitionFit: A call sign is the letters and numbers identifying a radio station or transmitter.

clue.text: Surreal essay across issue's front pages

indicators.note: the essay word spreads across, around, the other letters

parts.note: to essay is to attempt, a try

indicators.note: an issue's front is its first letter

explanation.surface: An odd essay is printed across the front pages of a magazine issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' looks like a noun for writing but is the verb meaning attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Trippy describes something weird and dreamlike, as if seen on a hallucinogenic drug trip.

to ease is to relieve

clue.text: Highly sensitive time for prayer, situation that's awkward in retrospect

parts.note: terce is the canonical hour of prayer at the third hour of the day

explanation.definitionFit: Top secret is the highest classification for sensitive, confidential information.

clue.text: Demolishing cored pears, set aside fuzzy skin

indicators.note: demolishing means these letters are knocked out of the longer word

parts.note: to supersede is to set aside or replace

indicators.note: cored means the centre letter of pears is removed

explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped, velvety surface, a skin with a fuzzy feel.
